Nanhe · design exploration · Nov 2026

Two ways to make Nanhe feel more baby

The logo, colours and type stay as they are. Only the packs and page graphics change. Below is the same bottle four ways, then each direction applied to the full line.

ALittle friends

A baby animal on every pack

Nine Indian animals, one per product, each chosen for a reason. The character replaces the ingredient drawing on the label, sits on the wipes lid, and peeks over the category arches. Each one has a Hindi pet name that parents and children can use.

What it does well

  • Gives the brand something no competitor has. "The elephant one" is easy to remember and ask for.
  • The Indian animals and Hindi names, Susu the river dolphin especially, make the brand clearly local without looking old-fashioned.
  • Characters carry over easily to social media, stickers, bath toys and a mascot.

Watch out for

  • The packs read younger, closer to a children's brand than a clinical one. The seal and back label have to do more of the trust work.
  • These drawings show the idea. For print, an illustrator should redraw them in this style.
  • Each new product needs a new animal, which takes more work to keep consistent.
BNight nursery

Moons, stars, clouds and rainbows

A soft repeating pattern in the category colour covers each pack. The label sits on a cloud-topped panel, and the category arches become rainbows. It feels like a nursery wall, without characters.

Moisturise pattern

Care & Protect pattern

Everyday Hygiene pattern

Bath & Toiletries pattern

Diapering pattern

What it does well

  • Calm and soft, and it still looks premium and clinical.
  • Extends to any new product with no new artwork. The pattern does the work.
  • The pattern works well on tissue paper, gift boxes and the website.

Watch out for

  • Moons, stars and rainbows are common in baby care, so this won't stand out much on a shelf.
  • The busy background competes with the label, which is why the label needs its own cloud panel.
My recommendation

Go with A, Little friends

The characters are the only one of these ideas that Nanhe could own, and the nine Indian animals tie straight back to the name. Direction B is lovely but generic: it makes the packs softer without making them more recognisable. Using both at once makes the packs look busy, as the fourth bottle at the top shows.

If A feels too young, a middle path is to keep today's clean packs and use the characters only on the wipes lid, the gift box, social media and the website.
